scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Hakken emerged in the early 1990s Dutch rave scene, especially in Rotterdam and The Hague, linked to the hardcore and gabber music culture.
The dance evolved from movements seen in Feyenoord football stadium stands, where fans mimicked mounting horses.
The name derives from the Dutch verb 'hakken,' meaning to chop or hack, referencing the heel-driven steps.
on_screen: Map: Netherlands · Europe

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Hakken is a social dance within rave and hard dance communities, expressing energy and connection to the music.
It is not sacred or ritualistic and has no known restrictions on participation.
The dance symbolizes the hardcore rave culture of 1990s Netherlands and its international offshoots.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Hakken is danced to hakmuziek, a style of hardcore and gabber music characterized by fast tempos (up to 190 BPM) and pounding bass drums.
The music's relentless bass drum beat dictates the rapid heel-driven footwork.
Listen for the Electronic drum machine (bass drum), Synthesizers.
The pulse is 4/4 at about 170 beats a minute.
A relentless pounding bass drum at high tempo drives the music, with electronic synth layers and occasional vocal samples creating an intense, energetic atmosphere.

Hakken is performed in rave venues, festivals, and club settings, often in groups but also solo.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Hoeppi Hakken is noted for influencing hakken by incorporating a backstep into the dance.
Andrea Limongelli Hakken is another individual associated with hakken, contributing to its development.
Australian hakken, often pronounced 'hack,' is danced to rawstyle music and features stylistic differences from Dutch hakken.
Hakken descends from European folk dance traditions involving foot stomping and tapping, adapted into the Dutch hardcore rave context.

scenes.title: Family tree

Hakken is variant of Freestyle hakken: Italian variant incorporating freestyle movements beyond traditional hakken.
